title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 87 (Rectification of the register of charges)

content.overview: The Central Government may direct extension of time or rectification of an omission/misstatement in charge-related filings only when satisfied that the omission/misstatement was accidental, due to inadvertence or other sufficient cause, or was not of a nature to prejudice creditors or shareholders. An application may be made by the company or a person interested.
content.glance: The Central Government may direct extension of time or rectification of an omission/misstatement in charge-related filings only when satisfied that the omission/misstatement was accidental, due to inadvertence or other sufficient cause, or was not of a nature to prejudice creditors or shareholders. An application may be made by the company or a person interested.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 87 (Rectification of the register of charges). The Central Government may, on an application by the company or a person interested, and on terms it considers just and expedient, direct extension of time for giving intimation of payment or satisfaction of a charge, or rectification of an omission/misstatement in a filing relating to a charge, its modification, a memorandum of satisfaction or an entry under section 82 or 83. It must be satisfied that the omission or misstatement was accidental, due to inadvertence or another sufficient cause, or was not of a nature to prejudice the position of creditors or shareholders. The power is conditional and is not an unrestricted authority to alter charge records. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Covered omission or misstatement
sections.body: The section addresses failure to give the Registrar intimation of payment or satisfaction of a charge within the required time, or omission/misstatement of particulars in a filing concerning a charge, its modification, a memorandum of satisfaction or an entry under section 82 or 83.

sections.heading: Qualifying grounds
sections.body: The Central Government must be satisfied that the omission or misstatement was accidental, due to inadvertence or another sufficient cause, or was not of a nature to prejudice the position of creditors or shareholders of the company.

sections.heading: Applicant and relief
sections.body: On application by the company or a person interested, and on terms and conditions it considers just and expedient, the Central Government may extend the time for giving the relevant intimation or direct rectification of the omission or misstatement.

examples.body: The Central Government may extend time or rectify an omission or misstatement in the register of charges where it is just and equitable.

hypotheticals.question: A company omitted to notify the Registrar of satisfaction of a charge within the prescribed time because of inadvertence. What does section 87 require?
hypotheticals.analysis: The company or a person interested may apply. The Central Government must be satisfied that the omission was accidental, due to inadvertence or other sufficient cause, or was not of a nature to prejudice creditors or shareholders. It may then extend time on appropriate terms.

hypotheticals.question: Can section 87 be used to rectify any inaccurate charge filing without further conditions?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The section requires the Central Government to be satisfied about the statutory grounds and allows relief on terms and conditions it considers just and expedient.

distinctions.title: Rectification and routine charge filing
distinctions.left: Section 87 is a conditional relief route for specified omissions/misstatements or late intimation of payment/satisfaction.
distinctions.right: Ordinary charge creation, modification or satisfaction filings must still follow the applicable statutory filing provisions and deadlines.

rows.left: Central Government on application by company/person interested
rows.right: Company files with Registrar under the relevant provision

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 87 as an unrestricted power to amend any charge entry.
misconceptions.correction: The section applies to specified charge-related omissions/misstatements and requires satisfaction of the statutory grounds.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming only the company can apply.
misconceptions.correction: The section permits an application by the company or a person interested.
The Central Government must be satisfied that the omission was accidental/inadvertent/sufficiently caused or not of a nature to prejudice creditors or shareholders.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 87 require?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: The Central Government may extend time or rectify an omission or misstatement in the register of charges where it is just and equitable.
